enriched.title: Vocabulário de Negócios e Termos Econômicos em Inglês
enriched.summary: A aula foca no ensino de vocabulário relacionado a negócios, economia e empreendedorismo, incluindo termos como precificação, juros, impostos e barris de petróleo. Também aborda a pronúncia correta de palavras-chave e apresenta exemplos práticos para fixação.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of money expected, required, or given in payment for something.
examples: The price of oil has increased significantly.
What is the price of this product?

vocabulary.definition: The act of setting a price for a product or service.
examples: Pricing strategies are critical for business success.
The company is reevaluating its pricing model.

vocabulary.definition: Having a significant or powerful effect.
examples: Her speech was very impactful.
The campaign had an impactful result on the community.

vocabulary.definition: Despite being aware of something.
examples: Even knowing the risks, they decided to invest.
She helped him even knowing it could be dangerous.

vocabulary.definition: Anxious or troubled about actual or potential problems.
examples: She was worried about the presentation.
He looked worried when he received the call.

vocabulary.definition: Relating to politics, especially international relations, as influenced by geographical factors.
examples: The geopolitical climate affects global markets.
Geopolitical tensions have risen in recent years.

vocabulary.definition: A unit of measurement for oil, equal to 42 US gallons.
examples: The price of an oil barrel has increased significantly.
They export thousands of oil barrels every day.

vocabulary.definition: Estimated or forecast based on current trends or data.
examples: The projected growth rate is 3% for next year.
The profits are projected to double by 2025.

vocabulary.definition: Planned or created with a specific purpose in mind.
examples: This program was designed to help students.
The house was designed by a famous architect.

vocabulary.definition: Eliciting admiration through size, quality, or skill.
examples: The view from the mountain is impressive.
Her performance was truly impressive.

vocabulary.definition: Used to express regret or sadness about an event or fact.
examples: Unfortunately, we missed the train.
Unfortunately, the event was canceled due to rain.

vocabulary.definition: A person who starts and manages a business, taking on financial risks.
examples: The entrepreneur launched a successful startup.
She is a well-known entrepreneur in the tech industry.

vocabulary.definition: The activity of setting up a business and taking on financial risks in the hope of profit.
examples: Entrepreneurship is key to a growing economy.
She studied entrepreneurship at university.

vocabulary.definition: Having the qualities or characteristics of an entrepreneur.
examples: He has an entrepreneurial mindset.
Her entrepreneurial spirit drives her success.

vocabulary.definition: A compulsory contribution to state revenue, levied by the government.
examples: Taxes are collected annually.
The new tax policy was implemented last year.

vocabulary.definition: The proportion of a loan charged as interest to the borrower.
examples: The interest rate for this loan is 5%.
Lower interest rates boost borrowing.

vocabulary.definition: A payment made to a professional person or institution for services.
examples: The lawyer charges a high fee for consultations.
There is a monthly fee for this service.

vocabulary.definition: The use of borrowed capital for investment, expecting the profits to be greater than the interest payable.
examples: The company used financial leverage to expand.
Leverage can increase returns but also risks.

vocabulary.definition: An amount of money borrowed by one party from another.
examples: He is struggling to pay off his debts.
The company is in debt to several banks.

vocabulary.definition: An entry recording an amount owed, listed on the left-hand side of an account.
examples: The bank debited $50 from my account.
Please check the debit column for errors.

culturalNotes: O vocabulário econômico é amplamente utilizado no inglês de negócios e é essencial para transações globais.
studyTips: Pratique a pronúncia das palavras em voz alta para internalizar os sons.
Crie frases próprias com o vocabulário aprendido para reforçar o uso prático.
originalExamples: The price of oil has increased significantly. (O preço do petróleo aumentou significativamente.)
The entrepreneur launched a successful startup. (O empreendedor lançou uma startup de sucesso.)
The company used financial leverage to expand. (A empresa utilizou alavancagem financeira para expandir.)
